T O: The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees, Finance and Facilities Committee FROM: Marc B.
Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng., President DATE: October 27, 2025 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval of FY2025 Audited Financial Statements P urpose of Submittal: This is a request to recommend to the full Board of Trustees the approval of the University of Rhode Island's audited Fiscal Year (FY) 2025 Financial Statements.
R ecommendation: It is recommended that the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees approve the University's FY 2025 Financial Statements.
P oints to Consider: URI’s external auditors, CliftonLarsonAllen LLP, have completed their audit and have no audit findings.
The University will have a clean audit opinion for the year ending June 30, 2025.
Upon approval by the URI Board of Trustees, the FY2025 financial statements will be issued.
P lease refer to pages 4-20 of the enclosed financial statements for the University’s Management's Discussion and Analysis, which provides a summary of the University’s FY2025 statements.

A few highlights are outlined below. • The University reported an increase in net position of $65.90 million in FY2025, up from $45.56 million in FY2024.
This includes a $20.13 million decrease in net position before $86.03 million in capital contributions, which significantly contributed to the overall increase.
Capital contributions largely represent investments from the State of Rhode Island in university assets (e.g., RICAP funding, G.O.
Bond revenues). • When reviewing the University’s condensed statement of revenues, expenses, and changes in net position, it is important to note that nonoperating revenue plays an important role in supporting the operations of the University.
The primary component of nonoperating revenues is State appropriations. • In FY2025, operating revenues decreased by $9.33 million (1.8%), compared to an $18.01 million (3.6%) increase in FY2024.
This decline is primarily due to a change in NACUBO reporting guidance that increased the scholarship allowance ( which nets against tuition and fees ).
Although this change reduced reported operating revenues, it did not impact overall operating income , as it involved a reclassification of existing expenses.

• Gross tuition and fee revenue increased by $4.36 million due to an increase in tuition rates of 3.6% for in- state students and 3.9% for out-of-state students, offset by a slight decrease in enrollment due in part to a problematic 2024-2025 FAFSA rollout which resulted in reduced application rates and delayed financial aid offers causing uncertainty for students seeking financial aid. • The operating expenses for the University increased by $25.30 million (3.8%) in FY2025, compared to a $37.76 million (6.1%) increase in FY2024. • The 2025 operating loss increased by $34.63 million from the prior year, as operating expenses increased by $25.30 million (3.8%), outpacing operating revenues that dipped by 1.8% from the prior year.
A significant portion of the expense increase was attributed to salaries and benefits, which, coupled with other operating expenses, accounted for most of the total rise in operating costs.
This was primarily due to position-related investments made in FY2 4 and FY25, along with cost -of-living salary adjustment s ranging from 2.5% to 5.0%. • The State’s unrestricted appropriation represents the largest component of the University’s nonoperating revenues.
